tools.name: check_connect
tools.description: After a download was refused with a connect link and code (download_limit without a key) and the user says they connected: returns api_key once they pressed Connect, made on their free account. Call it once after their reply, not in a loop: while status is pending, show them the link and code again and end your turn. Save the key as SFXMINT_API_KEY in the project's .env (gitignored), never in source, and retry the download with Authorization: Bearer <api_key>.

tools.name: create_listen_page
tools.description: Make a listening page for the user when choosing sounds for several events (a whole app or game): your candidates grouped by event, about three each, your recommendation first. The user opens listen_url, plays each one, picks one per event, can leave a note (“lower”, “shorter”) and presses Done; then call get_picks. Give the user listen_url before downloading anything for those events; if they say “you decide”, download your recommendations instead. Sounds are slugs from search_sounds, get_role_sound or get_sound_set. The page works for 24 hours; with an API key only this key's account reads the picks back. Up to 40 events of 1–5 sounds.

title.description: The project in a few words, shown on the page, e.g. 'Platformer: forest level'

label.description: Optional: how the page names it

recommended.description: Optional: your pick among sounds (the first when left out)

tools.name: generate_sound
tools.description: Make an individual sound effect from a description when the library has nothing suitable (search_sounds has no full match and its closest sounds do not suit). Needs an SFXMint API key on an account with AI-made sounds left in a pack: each take uses one AI-made sound per started 5 seconds, charged when it starts, and failed takes are given back. Without a key or AI-made sounds it answers with buy_url; the user decides whether to buy, an agent never pays. Returns WAV files (16-bit stereo, 44.1 kHz or 48 kHz as sample_rate asks; signed links valid 15 minutes) with SHA-256, MP3 (128 kbps) through the same link with ?format=mp3, and ogg_url; if they are not ready within about 25 seconds, it returns the order id for get_generation. Not CC0: the user may use them in their own projects, commercially, but not redistribute them as standalone sound files or in a sound collection. AI-generated: the user should listen before use.

prompt.description: What should be heard, in plain English (other languages are translated), at most 400 characters: the source, the action, the material, how it starts and ends. Mention only sounds to be heard.

duration_s.description: Length of each take in seconds; leave it out and SFXMint chooses from the description. Each started 5 seconds uses one AI-made sound a take.

variations.description: How many takes (default 2); each is charged

follow.description: How closely the takes follow the words: variety (default, for a short description), balanced, or close (for a detailed one); same price

sample_rate.description: The WAV's sample rate: 44100 (default) or 48000, the rate video and most game engines mix at; 16-bit stereo either way; same price

tools.name: get_generation
tools.description: Check a generation started with generate_sound, generate_ambience, generate_music or change_sound: status, kind and fresh download links for the finished takes, including loop_url when a loop was made.

order_id.description: The order_id returned by generate_sound, generate_ambience, generate_music or change_sound

tools.name: get_picks
tools.description: Read back a listening page's picks (create_listen_page): for each event the sound the user chose, their note, and what downloading it costs today: again (downloaded today), kept (credits keep it), free (within today's free downloads), credit (one of the account's download credits) or short (past both). Takes the API key of the account that made the page. status says whether the user pressed Done; until then ask them to finish on the page. When short is above 0, pass the next message on as it is, pay_url included, and download the rest; never pay yourself.

tools.name: get_role_sound
tools.description: Choose this when the task calls for a sound for a named event or interaction — a button click, purchase success, error beep, level-up, dialogue blip, notification. Pass the role as plain words: role ids (click, success, purchase-success, dialogue-blip, notification…) and common aliases (button click, ka-ching, jump scare, text blip…) are all accepted. Returns a qualified candidate for that role when one satisfies the requested constraints, with MP3 and WAV URLs, 2-3 alternates and the family page for browsing more. Free downloads are WAV or MP3 alike, counted by sound, not format. Download selected files locally and retain originals. Task-permitted processing requires a recipe, output SHA256, renewed file checks and a listening check. Other task-permitted sources or local synthesis may be mixed in. Optional style: crisp (short, bright, dry), soft (darker, gentler), spacious (reverb, longer tail), balanced (default: most typical). For multiple events consider get_sound_set; use search_sounds for a description or a gap. These are task branches, not a fixed sequence. Unknown roles return not_found with the full role list; GET https://sfxmint.com/api/v1/roles lists roles with aliases.

role.description: Role id or alias, e.g. 'click', 'button click', 'purchase-success', 'ka-ching', 'error beep', 'level-up', 'dialogue blip', 'notification'

style.description: Optional. balanced (default) = the family's most typical take; crisp = short, bright, dry; soft = darker, gentler; spacious = reverb, longer tail

max_duration_ms.description: Hard maximum length of the sound in milliseconds: a file may run longer with near-silence after the sound (audible_ms is the sound, duration_ms the file; checks say which was met).

loop.description: Require prepared loop metadata; seam evidence is returned separately.

format.description: Delivery format the candidate must have (ogg = Ogg Vorbis, only sounds published before 2026-10-14 have it); default MP3 and WAV URLs.

tools.name: get_sound
tools.description: Get full metadata for one sound by slug, including download URLs, description and acoustics measured from the WAV (silence before the sound, where it peaks, audible length, attack, tail, brightness, levels, character labels).

tools.name: get_sound_set
tools.description: Get a coherent set of sounds for an app or game in one call — one sound per role, with format metadata, hashes and stable download URLs. Use it when the task needs a whole kit; use get_role_sound for one event. Listen to the files in context. Sets include UI styles, game and app scenarios (fantasy-rpg covers spells, combat, loot, quests and level-up), acoustic-drum-kit, animal-calls (15 isolated calls), and dungeon-traps (6 isolated mechanisms). With an API key the answer also has credits: new_sounds (not kept yet) and credits_left on the account; tell the user before downloading more new sounds than credits_left.

format.description: File format for selection and checks (default WAV; WAV and MP3 download free alike; OGG only among sounds published before 2026-10-14). Legacy urls remains MP3; download_urls follows this format.

set.description: Set id (default ui-crisp). Includes acoustic-drum-kit, animal-calls and dungeon-traps alongside the UI and scenario sets listed in the enum.

tools.name: search_sounds
tools.description: Free-text search over the SFXMint library of free CC0 sound effects. Use it for sound descriptions, additional constraints or gaps left by another tool. Choose get_role_sound for a named event or get_sound_set for multiple events when that fits the task; these are task branches, not a fixed sequence. Hard constraints (duration, loop, format, excluded words) always apply. results hold sounds whose text has every word of the query. When there are none, closest lists the nearest sounds that meet every hard constraint, best first, each with missing_terms: judge them from title and description and let the user listen. library_fit says how well the library covers the request (full, close, weak, none). Returns direct, hotlinkable MP3 and WAV URLs and verified OGG (Vorbis) URLs where available, no attribution required, plus acoustics measured from the WAV (onset_ms, peak_ms, audible_ms, attack_ms, tail_ms, centroid_hz, peak_dbfs, rms_dbfs), envelope (16 equal slices of the file, 0–100) and bands (percent of energy low <250 Hz, mid, high >4 kHz) to tell candidates apart before the user listens, character labels like 'bright · punchy · tight', loop/file-QC status, and score/match as ranking evidence only (role = known role default, exact = all words hit, partial = some words hit, semantic = nearest by meaning). Free downloads are WAV or MP3 alike, counted by sound, not format. A measured one-shot with silence before or after it also has trimmed_mp3_url and trimmed_wav_url: the same sound without that silence, counted as the same sound.

query.description: Use concise English search terms for the source or event, action and essential audible traits from the user's request or project context: 'door slam', 'soft UI confirmation chime', 'coin pickup'. A single clear source such as 'thunder' is valid; do not pad it. Translate other languages while preserving meaning. Avoid full generation prompts, app backstory, synonym lists and invented materials or environments: full matches must cover every query word. Put duration, loop and format requirements in their separate fields. If no full match exists, inspect closest and missing_terms; simplify only optional wording, never silently drop a required trait.

category.description: Optional category slug: ui, retro-game, transition, impact, ambience, water, fire-electric, footsteps, door, mechanical, paper-fabric, glass, animal, crowd, cartoon, magic-scifi, horror, feedback, instrument, office, human, vehicle, household

max_duration_ms.description: Hard maximum length of the sound in milliseconds: a file may run longer with near-silence after the sound (audible_ms is the sound, duration_ms the file; checks say which was met).

loop.description: Require (true) or exclude (false) a candidate marked with prepared loop metadata; seam evidence is returned separately.

format.description: Delivery format (ogg = Ogg Vorbis, only sounds published before 2026-10-14 have it); loop=true defaults to WAV when omitted.
